description: Non-idealities of the quad-pendulum rigs (assumed values for small hobby/lab hardware; nominal, min, max and unit per rig). One shared definition for the classical designs (design/quadlib.py: realistic_rig, sample_realism, the firmware replica) and the RL domain randomisation (plan/RL_PLAN.md, step R1). Uniform sampling between min and max; parameters with min == max are fixed. 'per' says what one value applies to. Encoder layout: the encoder of joint k (AS5048-class magnetic, 14 bit) has its board on the body below the joint (the cart or arm tip for joint 1, else the distal end of link k-1) and its magnet on link k at the pivot; every board has its own cable down the chain to the base, so link k carries the cables of the encoders above it (n - k cables) and joint k is crossed by n - k cables. Cable springs are neutral at the upright (relative joint angle 0, base at 0).

cart.actuator: belt-driven servo motor: GT2 belt on a 20-tooth pulley, 40 mm of cart travel per motor revolution, 5 pole pairs

com_shift.description: Shift of each tube's own centre of mass towards its tip, as a fraction of the link length

base_mass_scale.description: Scale of the cart mass (carriage, belt clamp, cable carrier share)

b_joint.description: Viscous friction of a pendulum joint

tc_joint.description: Coulomb (breakaway) friction of a pendulum joint, typical small ball bearings; smooth form tc tanh(w / eps_joint). The screen (screen_results.json) finds this range too high for the quad: the cart needs <= 5e-5 per joint (selected low-friction bearings), the rotary quad fails from 2e-5

eps_joint.description: Velocity scale of the smooth Coulomb law (numerical, fixed)

b_base.description: Viscous friction of the carriage, belt and motor

tc_base.description: Coulomb friction of the linear guide carriage, belt and motor

eps_base.description: Velocity scale of the smooth Coulomb law (numerical, fixed)

m_enc_board.description: Encoder board with connector and screws (on the body below the joint)

m_enc_magnet.description: Diametric magnet and holder (on the link above, at the pivot)

rho_cable.description: Mass per length of one encoder cable (6-wire SPI)

k_cable.description: Bending stiffness of one cable loop across a pendulum joint

b_cable.description: Damping of one cable loop across a pendulum joint

k_cable_base.description: Spring of the cable carrier along the rail

b_cable_base.description: Damping of the cable carrier along the rail

joint_bits.description: Resolution of a joint encoder (AS5048-class: 2 pi / 16384 = 3.8e-4 rad)

joint_noise.description: White angle noise of a joint encoder before quantisation (assumed for an AS5048-class sensor; check the datasheet of the part used)

base_res.description: Cart position resolution: servo motor encoder through the belt (incremental 1000 lines x4 = 4000 counts per 40 mm)

base_noise.description: Cart position noise (an incremental encoder has none beyond its resolution)

delay.description: Whole-sample delay from sampling to the applied current: sample, compute, PWM update (integer)

tau_current.description: Time constant of the current (torque) loop after the delay

ripple_rel.description: Commutation torque ripple, relative to the command

ripple_per_rev.description: Ripple periods per motor revolution (6 x 5 pole pairs)

cogging.description: Cogging force at the cart (motor cogging torque over the pulley radius)

cogging_per_rev.description: Cogging periods per motor revolution (10 poles, 12 slots)

motor_per_base.description: Motor angle per cart travel (2 pi per 40 mm)

push.description: Tip push perpendicular to the top link (RL episodes; the balance design survives 0.037 N)

rotary.actuator: direct-drive gimbal BLDC on the arm hub (12 slots, 14 poles, 7 pole pairs), AS5048-class encoder on the shaft

eps_joint.description: Velocity scale of the smooth Coulomb law (numerical, fixed)

b_base.description: Viscous friction of the arm bearing and motor

tc_base.description: Coulomb friction of the gimbal motor bearings

eps_base.description: Velocity scale of the smooth Coulomb law (numerical, fixed)
